```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 14_anova_null_check
title: What would an F of 0.60 tell us?
questions:
  - id: below_one
    type: multiple-choice
    prompt: >
      In another two-group study, $F = 0.60$. Which interpretation fits?
    options:
      - text: The between-groups mean square is smaller than the within-groups mean square.
        correct: true
      - text: The treatment effect is negative.
      - text: The calculation must be wrong, because F cannot be below 1.
    explanation: >
      Either mean square can come out larger through sampling error, so
      $F$ can fall below 1. It doesn't carry a sign telling us which group
      has the higher mean.
```
